## Purpose

This SOP establishes a single, program-wide standard for labeling field
samples, completing chain of custody (COC) documentation, and
transporting samples from the field to the laboratory [@usepa2002qapp;
@apha2012]. Consistent labeling prevents sample mix-ups, and a complete
chain of custody ensures that data are legally defensible and
scientifically traceable. These procedures apply to all sample types
(water, soil, sediment, biological tissue, air filters) collected by
the EA Program.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All environmental samples collected during EA Program
  field activities, whether analyzed in-house or submitted to an
  external laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Internal laboratory standards and reagents
  (labeled per [SOP-L005](../lab_sops/SOP-L005-chemical-inventory.qmd));
  data files and digital records (see
  [SOP-L801](../lab_sops/SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites, vehicles, and laboratory
  receiving areas (SGM 133, 134)


## Responsibilities

| Role                | Responsibility                                        |
|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Project Lead   | Approve sample ID scheme for each project; designate receiving personnel |
| Field Lead          | Verify labels and COC forms before leaving the field  |
| Trained Personnel   | Label samples and complete COC per this SOP           |
| Receiving Personnel | Accept custody, verify sample condition, log receipt  |
| New Students        | Complete training before independent sampling         |


## Definitions

- **Chain of custody (COC):** A documented, unbroken record of the
  collection, transfer, and possession of a sample from the moment of
  collection through final analysis or disposal; used to demonstrate
  sample integrity for legal or regulatory purposes [@usepa2002qapp].
- **Holding time:** The maximum elapsed time between sample collection
  and analysis within which the sample remains chemically stable and
  analytically valid; analyte- and preservative-specific
  (e.g., 6 h for E. coli, 28 d for nitrate in H~2~SO~4~) [@apha2012].
- **Preservative:** A chemical added to a sample container
  (e.g., H~2~SO~4~, HNO~3~, Na~2~S~2~O~3~) to prevent biological or
  chemical degradation of target analytes during transport and storage
  [@apha2012].
- **QA/QC sample:** A blank, duplicate, spike, or other
  quality-control sample collected alongside field samples to assess
  contamination, precision, and accuracy; documented on the COC form.
- **Sample ID:** A unique alphanumeric code assigned to a sample at
  the moment of collection; the primary key linking field records,
  labels, COC forms, and laboratory data.
- **Zero headspace:** A sample container filled completely with no
  air gap; required for volatile organic compound (VOC) samples to
  prevent loss of analytes to the headspace.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Some sample containers include chemical preservatives
  (sulfuric acid, nitric acid, sodium thiosulfate). Handle
  pre-preserved bottles with care. Refer to
  [SOP-L003](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
- **Physical:** Coolers loaded with ice and sample bottles can be
  heavy. Use proper lifting technique.
- **Biological:** Soil and water samples may contain pathogens. Wear
  nitrile gloves when handling samples.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (when handling preserved bottles)

### Required Training

- [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
- [SOP-F003 Field Notebook Protocols](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd)

## Procedure

### Sample ID Scheme

The PI or project lead establishes the sample ID scheme before the
first field outing. A standard EA Program sample ID has the structure:

```
[ProjectCode]-[SiteCode]-[YYYYMMDD]-[SampleType]-[Replicate]
```

Example: `SGMC-US1-20260415-GW-A`

Record the scheme in the project metadata file and in the field
notebook before the first sampling event.

### Labeling Sample Containers

1. Write the sample ID on the pre-printed label or directly on the
   container using a waterproof marker.
2. Include the following minimum fields on every label:
   - Sample ID
   - Collection date and time (24 h format)
   - Collector initials
   - Matrix (water / soil / sediment / tissue / air filter)
   - Preservative (if present)
3. For pre-preserved bottles, verify the preservative type is printed
   or written on the container before field use.
4. For biological samples requiring cold preservation, add an ice
   temperature indicator sticker.

### Completing the COC Form

1. Start a new COC form for each cooler.
2. Fill in all header fields: project name, project number, field
   lead, date, field site.
3. Enter each sample in the log: sample ID, matrix, collection date
   and time, preservative, number of containers, and requested
   analysis.
4. Include QA/QC samples (field blanks, field duplicates, trip blanks)
   on the same COC form as the associated samples.
5. Sign and date the form before departing the field.

### Sample Transport

1. Place samples in the cooler with sufficient ice to maintain 4 °C.
2. Separate chemically preserved bottles from unpreserved samples
   using a zip-lock bag as secondary containment.
3. Verify the cooler temperature on departure and on arrival using a
   thermometer; record both readings on the COC form.
4. Transport samples promptly; do not leave samples in a hot vehicle.

### Receiving Samples in the Laboratory

1. The receiving person checks the sample count against the COC form.
2. Verify that the number of containers matches the COC listing; note
   any discrepancies.
3. Check sample temperature with a thermometer placed among the
   bottles and record on the COC form.
4. Transfer samples to appropriate storage:
   - Water samples: refrigerator at 4 °C
     ([SOP-L106](../lab_sops/SOP-L106-refrigerators-freezers.qmd))
   - Soil samples: refrigerator at 4 °C (short-term) or freezer
     (archiving)
   - Biological samples: freezer at -20 °C or -80 °C as required
5. Both the field lead and the receiving person sign and date the COC
   form to document the transfer of custody.
6. File the signed COC form with the project records.


## Quality Control

- The field lead reviews all labels and the COC form before leaving
  the field site.
- Receiving personnel verify sample count, condition, and temperature
  upon arrival.
- Any broken, leaking, or incorrectly labeled samples are flagged on
  the COC form and reported to the PI within 24 hours.
- COC forms are retained for the duration of the project plus a
  minimum of 5 years.

## Training Record

Before labeling and handling samples independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-F003 Field Notebook Protocols](SOP-F003-field-notebook-protocols.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate correct sample labeling using the project ID scheme
3. Complete a COC form correctly during a supervised field outing
4. Be signed off by the field lead or PI
